clue.text: Old soldier volunteers without returning decoration

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's former volunteer reserve of soldiers, renamed in 2014

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so this word is read from right to left

parts.note: without, as in sugarless: lacking

explanation.surface: A veteran fails to come back and collect his medal or award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like a container signal, but here it means lacking. The Territorial Army was renamed the Army Reserve in 2014, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassel is a tuft of hanging threads used as an ornament on cushions, curtains or caps.

parts.note: taken as written
Rome as the Italians spell it

explanation.surface: A shopper buys scent abroad in some overseas city.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfume in the sense of a pleasant smell is a synonym of aroma.

clue.text: Wise suppressing cold anger and profanity

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down within, so one word sits inside another

parts.note: a sage is a wise person; also sage as an adjective
C for cold, as on a tap
to rile is to anger

explanation.surface: A wise person holds back their chilly fury and swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGE holds C and RILE together: SA + C + RILE + GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilege is disrespect toward sacred things, and profanity in its older sense means just that irreverence.

parts.note: lit is slang for intoxicated
the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A tipsy fellow has become remarkably bendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an anagram signal for 'the', but it is the word LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe describes a body that bends easily and moves with supple grace.

clue.text: Borders of short dress giving flash

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the two end letters of short
a robe is a long garment

explanation.surface: The hem of a skimpy frock is lit by a camera flashbulb.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a lamp producing rapid bursts of light, so a flash in noun form.

parts.note: surface reading: someone whose job is short-lived or temporary
setter's reading: a brief is the set of instructions given to a lawyer, and to brief one is to engage one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' reads as an adjective for short, but it is the legal noun or verb for instructing a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor is the English lawyer who takes clients' instructions and briefs barristers, so their work comes as briefs.

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter
the Ural flows from Russia to the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: Someone asks which nation a certain Russian river rises in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is used adjectivally, as in country life, to match the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural and country both describe the countryside as opposed to the town.

indicators.note: something thrashed is beaten about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: Someone told to fall into line, after a beating for not knowing better.
explanation.definitionFit: Benighted literally means overtaken by night, hence figuratively in intellectual darkness: unenlightened.

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upward, so this word runs backwards

parts.note: to peel is to strip off a layer

explanation.surface: A grown-up undresses on getting up, or perhaps in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that being in bed only usually means being unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asleep is typically lying in bed, so the definition is by example rather than synonym.

clue.text: Fellow admitting this compiler is humble

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a dean is a senior fellow of a college
the setter referring to themself

explanation.surface: A college fellow letting the setter in turns out to be modest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble' is the verb here, to bring low, matching demean.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, which is what humbling them does.

clue.text: Suffering terribly, one isn't complaining initially

definitions.text: Suffering terribly, one isn't complaining initially

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each word, so the opening letters are taken

parts.note: the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A sufferer in great pain refuses, at first, to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: someone in agony who will not complain is a stoic.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures pain or hardship without showing feeling, after the Greek philosophical school.

clue.text: Indulgence later on changed by church

indicators.note: letters that are changed are rearranged into a different order

parts.note: the anagram fodder
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A papal indulgence is later altered by the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indulgence' suggests the religious sense, fitting church, but here it means leniency.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgence in the sense of permissiveness or patience with others is a synonym of tolerance.

clue.text: Probe with tool turning over pit

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool
a mine is a coal pit

explanation.surface: An investigator uses an implement to dig over a mine shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe a matter is to inspect it closely, which is what examine means as a verb.

clue.text: Scent of pine outgrowth around trunk

indicators.note: around puts one word on both sides of another, enclosing it

parts.note: a pine cone grows on the tree
a log is a section of tree trunk

explanation.surface: A smell of pine wafts from something growing on a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne, short for eau de Cologne, is a light perfume, so a scent.

clue.text: Tie workers in empty plant job

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the following one
an empty word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters only
to lace is to tie up, as shoes
men as a workforce

explanation.surface: Factory staff knot something together inside an abandoned plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory in the surface; here only its two outer letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: A placement is a position or posting, especially temporary work experience: a job.

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for America
a do is a party
a ration is a portion or serving

explanation.surface: The USA is applauded for its partying and food portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Praise' is a noun here, worship or homage, to match the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is reverent worship, and praise in the sense of honour given to God overlaps it.

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A tenancy agreement goes unchanged, provided the tenant gets a door key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a noun for a door, but it is the adjective meaning crucial.
explanation.definitionFit: Key as an adjective means of central importance, which is what essential means.

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as two words: staged a sit-in protest, one possible way of demonstrating
second meaning: a smooth glossy fabric

explanation.surface: Perhaps a demonstration was given of some shiny cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning reads the answer as two words, SAT IN: protesters at a sit-in demonstrate by sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a glossy woven fabric, and its sheen makes slick a fair description of it.

clue.text: Dubious Celt with cap is ridiculous

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A doubtful Scot or Irishman in a silly hat looks absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: Celt is a member of the Celtic peoples, such as the Scots, Irish or Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious can mean doubtful in attitude, as in being unsure of a claim, which matches sceptical.

clue.text: Excited all right, gripped by admiration

indicators.note: to be gripped by something is to be held inside it

parts.note: awe is reverent wonder
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled and fine, held spellbound by wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' is a past-tense verb, roused, matching awoke.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite in its old sense is to stir or rouse, and something roused has woken.

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: ale is beer
a sac is a bladder-like pouch in the body

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to drink with bladder full for some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the answer is a region that makes wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is the French wine region bordering Germany, famous for Riesling and Gewürztraminer.

indicators.note: taking in means accepting inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: the comparative of sure
to rend is to tear apart

explanation.surface: Quitting a job looks a safer bet while having a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' reads as a rest from work, but it is the verb rend.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign in the sense of giving something up, such as a claim, is to surrender it.

clue.text: Face wreathed in cares is tired

indicators.note: to be wreathed in something is to be surrounded by it, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: running across the three words

explanation.surface: A careworn, weary expression bears the lines of worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like a noun, the worn countenance, but it is the verb to oppose.
explanation.definitionFit: To face an attack or pressure is to stand up against it, which is to resist it.

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap around, so one letter sits inside

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
N for northern

explanation.surface: A calm stretch of water will shortly cover the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Anon is an old-fashioned word for soon, as in 'more anon'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland and the British Isles.

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: nice means pleasant or sweet
the heart of sweet: its middle letter, a standard crossword trick

explanation.surface: A family member is lovely, cuddling her boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweetheart is split: sweet + heart, its centre letter going inside the word for sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family member, the daughter of a sibling, so a relative.

indicators.note: welcoming means letting in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: pious means devout

indicators.note: disheartened means with its heart removed, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: outer letters of the

explanation.surface: A holy person takes in the downcast and miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The disheartened' looks like a noun phrase for depressed people, but it means the word 'the' minus its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Piteous means deserving or arousing pity, which is what wretched describes.

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a po is a chamberpot, so its plural
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Bedroom chamberpots, unpleasant and stinking.
explanation.walkthrough: A po (from French pot) is a chamberpot, a bowl kept under the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pongs is British slang for stinks, a verb or plural noun matching smells.

parts.note: O looks like zero
deal is softwood timber such as pine, so pine is an example of deal

explanation.surface: A card player announces no bid before dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' suggests cards, but it is fir or pine timber; 'say' marks pine as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, which is to declare a view.

clue.text: Model is caught before interior shot

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A fashion model is photographed ahead of an indoor shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' and 'shot' suggest photography; shot is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a standard for judging, and a model in the sense of a standard to follow matches it.

clue.text: One ambushed by criminal's getting coppers

indicators.note: someone ambushed is surrounded and trapped, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: con is a convict, plus the S of the possessive
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man waylaid by a crook ends up being arrested by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like the police, but it means copper coins, Britain's pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppers are low-value bronze or copper coins, so coins is the general term.

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned 1702 to 1714
perfect in the sense of complete or total

explanation.surface: A monarch who almost never loses her cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like a mood but is the metalworking verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal metal or glass is to heat and slowly cool it to toughen it, which is tempering.

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so one letter is placed inside the word

parts.note: a saver is someone who collects money or things
L for large, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A collector gets hold of a big dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A salver is a flat tray, often of silver, used for serving, so a kind of plate.
